After a config change on router6, traffic destined to subnets that
are not in router6's RIP-learned table fails. Local intra-Location-B
traffic still works, and RIP-learned destinations (172.16.10.0/24,
192.168.100.0/24, etc.) are reachable. But router6 itself can no
longer reach any external/unknown destination. Diagnose what was
removed on router6.

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router6 default route
Mechanism: router6 has RIP-learned routes for the topology's
  internal prefixes, but anything outside that scope (e.g.
  8.8.8.8, external WAN destinations) relied on the static
  default route via 10.50.1.1. Without it, router6 drops any
  packet whose destination is not in its RIB.
  Intra-Location-B traffic is unaffected because router6 has
  directly-connected / RIP-learned routes for those prefixes.
  (Note: Location B -> Location A is independently blocked by
  router6's WAN-side ACL 110, so do NOT use cross-Location
  pings as a test signal here.)
Localization: router6
Root cause: default route missing on router6
Fix: `ip route add default via 10.50.1.1 metric 150` on router6
scenario.fix_spec: `ip route add default via 10.50.1.1 metric 150` on router6

agent.diagnosis_text:
- Affected component: Router6’s control-plane routing (FRR/zebra) lost its default (0.0.0.0/0) route.
- Mechanism: Router6 still has connected routes (172.18.50.0/24, 172.18.51.0/24, 10.50.1.0/24) and RIP-learned prefixes via 10.50.1.1, so traffic to known/RIP destinations works. For any destination not explicitly in the RIB, the kernel requires a default route. With no default present, such traffic is dropped locally at router6, matching the symptom “router6 itself can no longer reach any external/unknown destination.”
- Localization: On router6, uplink interface eth2 is 10.50.1.2 toward router3 (next hop 10.50.1.1). Evidence shows no default in either FRR or the kernel:
  • FRR routes: no 0.0.0.0/0, only R and C routes via 10.50.1.1.
  • Kernel table: ip route shows no “default” entry.
  • FRR running config contains only “router rip … network 10.0.0.0/8” and no “ip route 0.0.0.0/0 …”.
- Root cause: The static default route (0.0.0.0/0 via 10.50.1.1 on eth2) was removed from router6’s FRR configuration.
- Corrective fix: Re-add the default route so unknown destinations forward to the upstream router:
  In vtysh on router6:
    conf t
      ip route 0.0.0.0/0 10.50.1.1
    end
    write memory
Alternatively at OS level:
  ip route add default via 10.50.1.1 dev eth2
Persist it via FRR to survive reloads. After adding, router6 will again route external/unknown traffic via 10.50.1.1 while maintaining RIP-learned reachability.

per_axis.rationale: The submission explicitly identifies router6 as the affected device and localizes the issue to its control plane and interfaces.
The agent explicitly identifies the missing default (0.0.0.0/0) route on router6 as the affected component and root cause.
The diagnosis explicitly contrasts RIP-learned/connected routes (internal reachability) with the missing static/default (0.0.0.0/0) route for external destinations and explains the drop behavior.
Proposes re-adding the missing default route via 10.50.1.1 on router6 (in FRR or kernel) which restores external/unknown traffic forwarding as expected.

The agent's conclusion (missing default route on router6 leading to drops of external traffic) is plausible and mostly supported by the provided logs (running-config shows only RIP and no static default; agent notes claim no default in FRR/kernel). However the explicit route-table outputs proving the absence of a 0.0.0.0/0 entry are truncated/not visible, so some claims are asserted rather than fully shown.
